newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to issue T$3 bln NCDs on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to issue T$3 bln NCDs on Thursday.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Thursday it would issue T$3 billion in 14-day negotiable certificates of deposit (NCDs)later in the day.
Bids would close at 15.00 local time (0700 GMT), a central bank official said.
On Wednesday a central bank official said the resumption of NCD issues had nothing to do with movements in the stock market.
The bank issued T$5 billion in 14-day NCDs on Wednesday in a bid to mop up excess funds.
"The NCD issue was a response to the banking system's loose liquidity," said Lee Sheng-yen, a central bank director.
"It had nothing to do with stock market movements," Lee told reporters after the close of Taiwan's markets on Wednesday.
Wednesday's NCDs issue raised concerns that the central bank has resumed a drive to curb the loose liquidity that many analysts had said was fuelling a major stock market rally.
That rally has suffered a major setback since March 20, when announcement of a total pork export ban due to an epidemic of hog foot and mouth disease sent share prices tumbling.
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong on Monday pledged that the bank would take the economy's health into consideration in any further issues of the short-term instruments.
"We will not continue to blindly issue NCDs," Sheu said in the wake of the stock market's plunge on Monday. "We will do it in consideration of overall economic conditions."
The central bank had made major daily NCD issues almost every day up until March 21, when the stock market plunged more than three percent because of the farm crisis.
The stock market again fell dramatically on Monday and Tuesday over the pork crisis and worries of new frictions with rival China, but rebounded strongly on Wednesday.
The index rose early on Thursday.
